name: Dexto

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Rendered pricing links through /docs/pricing to Services billing: Sandbox managed compute $0.414/hour while running. CPU/RAM allocation not specified, so not normalized to 4/8.

Public API permits one primary Linux sandbox per user; repeated create returns the same resource. Pause stops active compute charges while retaining workspace; visual desktop is not a separate public API resource.
Free $5 one-time; Pro displayed $25 is top-up credit, not a monthly fee. Credits also fund tokens/media/connections; dedicated GPU/model services available on request.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
Credits are prepaid and non-refundable. The Pro top-up is $25 by default, adjustable from $5 to $500. No expiry is stated on the public pages.

fleet.notes: Public CPU sandbox API gives each user one primary sandbox; repeat POST returns that same sandbox rather than provisioning another. No multi-sandbox creation/raise path documented; none denotes current API single-primary restriction, not a promise that private enterprise arrangements can never exist. Sandbox lifecycle API rate limits: create/start/pause/delete/processes 60 requests per 60 s (sandbox_write), reads 300 per 60 s; each command runs at most 120 s (timeout_ms max 120000).

own_agent_api.quote: Use `autobots.send`, `autobots.status`, and `autobots.read` for conversations. Call `autobots.respond` only for a pending input or approval returned for that owned AutoBot.
own_agent_api.note: Only for Dexto's OWN agents (Dexto assistant / agent profiles / AutoBots), driven via the OAuth MCP server at https://app.dexto.ai/mcp ('Capabilities perform direct actions; Agents and AutoBots take on delegated work') or page-bound WebMCP tools on autobots.dexto.ai. The agent runs in the Dexto control plane and uses the cloud computer as its execution workspace, rather than being a harness process inside the sandbox. The REST API only lists agents (GET /api/agents); no REST endpoint to send prompts. No Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode harness driving. Separately, the open-source Dexto agent runtime (truffle-ai/dexto) has a self-hosted `dexto --mode server` 'REST & SSE APIs' mode, unrelated to the hosted sandbox.

image_oci.quote: Get or create your sandbox ... POST /v1/sandboxes ... The first call creates a paused sandbox and returns 201; later calls return the same primary sandbox with 200.
image_oci.note: Sandbox creation takes no image parameter; each user gets one fixed primary Linux workspace, not a chosen/custom OCI image.

docker_inside.quote: POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/processes ... The response contains exit_code, stdout, and stderr.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the documented API only exposes plain command execution and file I/O under /workspace, with no mention of Docker/containers inside.

nested_virt.quote: A CPU sandbox is a Linux workspace you can start when you need to run code.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no /dev/kvm or nested virtualization capability is documented for the CPU sandbox.

computer_use.quote: Use your API key with https://api.dexto.ai; the dashboard's visual desktop is not a separate public API resource.
computer_use.note: not offered: the visual desktop exists in the dashboard but there is no public screenshot/click API to drive it.

anti_bot.quote: Dexto has its own persistent cloud computer that it uses to store files, run code, open browsers and
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Dexto is an agent-work control plane, not a stealth/anti-detection browsing product.

captcha_solving.quote: Dexto has its own persistent cloud computer that it uses to store files, run code, open browsers and
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: Use your API key with https://api.dexto.ai; the dashboard's visual desktop is not a separate public API resource.
ssh.note: not offered: the only documented access paths are the REST processes/files endpoints; no SSH endpoint or credentials are documented.

snapshot.quote: Use POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/pause to stop charging for active compute while retaining its workspace.
snapshot.note: Pause just stops billing while keeping the persistent workspace; no snapshot/checkpoint API (disk or memory) is documented.

snapshot_auto.quote: Use POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/pause to stop charging for active compute while retaining its workspace.
snapshot_auto.note: No auto-snapshot-on-stop mechanism documented beyond simply retaining the workspace files.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: See /v1/openapi.json for the complete request and response schemas, errors, and rate limits.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint is listed in the documented sandbox API surface.

fork.quote: The first call creates a paused sandbox and returns 201; later calls return the same primary sandbox with 200.
fork.note: Each user has one primary sandbox and repeated create calls return that same resource; there is no clone/fork mechanism.

fork_running.quote: The first call creates a paused sandbox and returns 201; later calls return the same primary sandbox with 200.
fork_running.note: Follows from no fork capability at all.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The first call creates a paused sandbox and returns 201; later calls return the same primary sandbox with 200.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Follows from no fork/snapshot capability at all.

wake_on_request.note: Starting a paused sandbox requires an explicit start call; no documentation of automatic wake on an inbound request.

volume_attach.quote: All file paths must stay under /workspace, and the sandbox must already be running.
volume_attach.note: Only a single fixed /workspace path is documented; no attachable extra volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Each user currently has one primary sandbox.
volume_shared.note: With one primary sandbox per user and no volume API, a shared multi-machine volume is not offered.

live_resize.quote: Compute Sandbox ... Managed compute for agent runs. While running $0.414 / hour
live_resize.note: No vCPU/RAM sizing options or resize endpoint are documented; pricing is a single flat hourly rate.

agent_harnesses.quote: MCP setup: Connect Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, or Hermes through https://app.dexto.ai/mcp and OAuth.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Dexto connects to external coding harnesses via MCP rather than preinstalling harnesses like Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode inside its own sandbox.

harness_api.note: not offered: the REST API only lists agents; there is no first-party API to prompt/stream/follow-up a coding harness running inside the sandbox.

public_ipv4.quote: Use your API key with https://api.dexto.ai; the dashboard's visual desktop is not a separate public API resource.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the sandbox is reached only through the Dexto API, with no per-machine public IPv4 documented.

inbound_https.quote: See /v1/openapi.json for the complete request and response schemas, errors, and rate limits.
inbound_https.note: No documented way to expose an HTTPS URL to a port on the sandbox; only processes/files endpoints exist.

ingress_rules.quote: See /v1/openapi.json for the complete request and response schemas, errors, and rate limits.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; there is no exposed-port/ingress feature to control.

egress_http_rules.quote: A CPU sandbox is a Linux workspace you can start when you need to run code.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no method/path-level egress control is documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials remain inside platform-controlled execution paths; an agent receives the permitted tool surface, not a
secret_proxy.note: Connections keep third-party credentials inside Dexto's control plane for its own agents/capabilities, not a first-party HTTP proxy that injects secrets into arbitrary calls made from inside the CPU sandbox.

gpu.quote: Compute Sandbox ... Managed compute for agent runs. While running $0.414 / hour. Available on request: Self-hosted models and dedicated GPU access for your team.
gpu.note: not offered: the public Compute Sandbox is CPU-only ('CPU sandboxes API'); dedicated GPU access is a separate enterprise model-hosting offering, not a GPU sandbox/VM product.

windows.quote: A CPU sandbox is a Linux workspace you can start when you need to run code.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the sandbox is explicitly a Linux workspace.

macos.quote: A CPU sandbox is a Linux workspace you can start when you need to run code.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the sandbox is explicitly a Linux workspace.

self_host.quote: Dexto Cloud routes LLMs, image generation, voice and audio, video, open-source LLMs, and managed compute through one services catalog.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; the hosted Dexto Cloud sandbox/control plane has no documented self-hosting option (a separate, unrelated open-source truffle-ai/dexto agent runtime exists but is not this hosted sandbox product).

open_source.quote: Dexto Cloud routes LLMs, image generation, voice and audio, video, open-source LLMs, and managed compute through one services catalog.
open_source.note: The hosted Dexto Cloud control plane / sandbox product itself is not published as open source; only a separate, unrelated agent-runtime repo (truffle-ai/dexto) is open source.
